title: Striped QKV cooperative kernel and rotary parameter reorg for long-sequence throughput
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduce striped QKV layout + cooperative warp kernel and rotary parameter reorganization. Improves long-sequence throughput and reduces KV memory for large-batch workloads. Backwards-compatible execution paths retained; rolling rollout recommended.
description: Context: Long-attention workloads with uneven sequence length distributions expose inefficiencies in the QKV memory layout and warp utilization on modern GPUs. This PR implements a striped QKV layout and a cooperative-warp kernel that reduces memory reads/writes and increases SM utilization for sequences >2048 tokens. It also reorganizes rotary parameter storage to improve cache locality when applying rotary embeddings across sharded KV caches. Motivation: reduce end-to-end token latency and KV working set for Redwood's continuous-batching serving runtime while preserving correctness and compatibility with existing model artifacts. Summary of changes: - Striped QKV layout: memory layout change in the attention prepack step that lays out Q, K, V in a stripe-interleaved format to enable coalesced loads for the cooperative kernel. - Cooperative-warp kernel: a new CUDA kernel that schedules attention work across a warp group to avoid redundant loads and make better use of shared memory for KV pieces. - Rotary parameter reorg: change in rotary sin/cos packing to align with striped QKV words and reduce per-token computation overhead when applying rotary to cached KV. - Fallback path: non-striped path preserved for small sequence/batch shapes to avoid regressions. - Tests & Benchmarks: microbenchmarks for 2k/4k/8k sequences and end-to-end serving harness results with continuous batching. Checklist: - [x] Implementation of striped layout and kernel - [x] Unit tests for correctness (compare numeric closeness with baseline) - [x] Microbenchmarks for long sequences - [x] Stability gates in runtime to enable staged rollout - [ ] Docs: perf note and guidance (follow-up) Performance results (selected): - A100 (40GB), fp16, seq=8192, batch=16: throughput +22% (tokens/s) vs baseline; p50 token latency -11.3% - A100, seq=2048, batch=32: throughput +12%; p50 latency -6.8% - KV working set memory reduction ~18% for cached K/V frames on long-seq workloads - Small sequences (seq<=128): negligible delta (+/-1%), fallback path engaged for parity Safety/compatibility notes: backward-compatible API, no model file format changes. Rotary reorg is purely in-memory packing; rollout is gated behind a runtime feature flag (runtime.feature.striped_qkv_enabled). Linked work: ENG-4392 (striped-kv perf spike), ENG-4411 (rotary cache regression investigation). Implementation notes: - The kernel uses cooperative warp shuffles and shared memory staging for Q/K/V tiles; we bounded shared memory to 48KB to stay within typical node configs. - We added a runtime heuristic that enables striped path when (seq >= 1024 AND batch >= 8) OR (estimated kv_bytes_per_request > 50MB). - Added a small micro-benchmark harness (benchmarks/attn/longseq_bench.py) and CI job to run it on a perf runner. Migration/Rollout plan: - Merge behind feature flag - Deploy to perf canary cluster, run workload replay for 48h - Gradual rollout to Dedicated pools with traffic-split and automatic rollback if regressions detected Review notes & decisions: keep the non-striped fallback for small shapes; keep fp32 accumulator path unchanged for numerical parity; defer doc authoring to follow-up.
